paragraphs.english: Saki practiced a short piano piece for a class concert. She liked the opening and played it again and again. However, two bars in the middle were difficult. Each time she reached them, she stopped, felt unhappy, and returned to the beginning. After a week, she could play the opening beautifully, but the middle had hardly improved. She began to think that she was simply not good at music.
paragraphs.translation: サキはクラスの演奏会のため、短いピアノ曲を練習していた。冒頭が好きで、何度も繰り返し弾いた。しかし中間の二小節は難しかった。そこまで来るたび、手を止め、嫌な気持ちになり、冒頭へ戻った。一週間後、冒頭は美しく弾けたが、中間はほとんど上達していなかった。単に音楽が苦手なのだと思い始めた。

paragraphs.english: Her teacher asked her to play only the difficult bars very slowly. [1] Saki noticed that one finger had to move before the next note began. Once she understood the movement, she repeated it several times and then joined the bars to the rest of the piece. The whole song became smoother.
paragraphs.translation: 先生は、難しい小節だけをごくゆっくり弾くよう頼んだ。こうすることで、いつも最初からやり直さず、一つの小さな問題を詳しく調べられた。次の音が始まる前に、一つの指を動かす必要があると気づいた。その動きを理解すると、数回繰り返し、それからその小節を曲の残りにつなげた。曲全体がより滑らかになった。

paragraphs.english: She still practiced the opening, but she no longer spent all her time there. Her next week's plan gave extra time to the places that needed attention. Saki discovered that a useful practice session was not always the same as an enjoyable performance of the easiest part.
paragraphs.translation: 冒頭も練習し続けたが、もう全ての時間をそこに使わなかった。翌週の計画では、注意が必要な箇所に多めの時間を割いた。有用な練習は、最も簡単な部分を楽しく演奏することと必ずしも同じではないとサキは分かった。

paragraphs.english: The science club planned an evening for families to look at stars. Members borrowed two telescopes and made a list of bright objects to find. On the afternoon of the event, thick clouds covered the sky. Some members wanted to send everyone a cancellation message. Their leader asked whether the evening had to depend entirely on seeing real stars through a telescope.
paragraphs.translation: 科学部は、家族向けに星を見る夕べを計画した。部員は望遠鏡二台を借り、探す明るい天体の一覧を作った。行事当日の午後、厚い雲が空を覆った。何人かの部員は、全員に中止の連絡を送りたがった。部長は、その夕べが本物の星を望遠鏡で見ることに全面的に依存する必要があるか尋ねた。

paragraphs.english: They moved tables into the school hall and spread out large sky maps. [1] At one table, children practiced finding north on a map. At another, they learned how to hold and adjust the telescope without moving it toward the sky. Parents asked questions that the club had not expected.

paragraphs.english: A small island received parcels by boat three times a week. When visitors ordered things online, they sometimes expected delivery the next day. A shopkeeper named Nori often heard complaints when packages arrived later. The online message said that an order had left a warehouse, but it did not show when the island boat would leave the mainland. Strong winds could delay the boat even after a parcel reached the port.
paragraphs.translation: 小さな島は、週三回船で小包を受け取っていた。来訪者がネット注文すると、翌日に届くと思うことがあった。ノリという店主は、荷物が遅れるとよく苦情を聞いた。ネットの通知では注文品が倉庫を出たと分かったが、島行きの船がいつ本土を出るかは示されなかった。小包が港に着いた後でも、強風で船が遅れることがあった。

paragraphs.english: Nori made a small board beside his shop. [1] He wrote the next planned boat day and added a note when the port announced a change. He did not promise an exact arrival time for each parcel. Instead, the board helped people understand which part of the journey they were waiting for.
paragraphs.translation: ノリは店の横に小さな掲示板を作った。本土の港から届く最新情報を使った。次の予定運航日を書き、港が変更を発表すると注意書きを足した。小包ごとの正確な到着時刻を約束したわけではない。代わりに、人々が配送のどの段階を待っているか理解する助けになった。

paragraphs.english: Visitors began asking more useful questions. Rather than saying that the shop had lost their parcel, they asked whether the next boat was running. Nori could not change the wind, but clear local information made the wait less confusing for everyone.
paragraphs.translation: 来訪者は、より役立つ質問をし始めた。店が荷物をなくしたと言う代わりに、次の船が運航しているか尋ねた。風は変えられないが、分かりやすい地域の情報で、誰もが待ち時間の状況を理解しやすくなった。

title: 絵のついた昼食メニュー

paragraphs.english: At the beginning of the school year, students from several countries joined a lunch club. Each Friday, the members ordered meals from a small restaurant. Some students did not eat meat, and others preferred food without hot peppers. The restaurant had many choices, but its menu used words that new members did not know. Asking a friend to explain every dish took a long time. The club leader, Lisa, wanted everyone to choose a meal without feeling embarrassed. [1] She asked the restaurant owner to check each drawing before printing the new menu. A leaf showed meals without meat, and a pepper showed hot dishes. The pictures did not replace the names or descriptions. They helped students decide which descriptions to read carefully. At the next meeting, ordering took less time, and two new members asked questions about dishes they had never tried. Lisa realized that a small change in information could make joining a group easier.
paragraphs.translation: 新学年の初め、複数の国の生徒が昼食クラブに入った。毎週金曜、部員は小さな店から食事を注文した。肉を食べない生徒も、唐辛子抜きの料理がよい生徒もいた。店の選択肢は多かったが、メニューには新しい部員が知らない単語が使われていた。友人に全ての料理を説明してもらうのには、長い時間がかかった。部長のリサは、皆が気まずくならずに食事を選べるようにしたかった。料理名の横に簡単な絵を足そうと提案した。新メニューを印刷する前に、絵を一つずつ確認するよう店主に頼んだ。葉は肉なしの料理、唐辛子は辛い料理を表した。絵は料理名や説明に置き換わるものではなかった。どの説明をよく読むか決める助けになった。次の集まりでは注文が早まり、新しい部員二人が未経験の料理について質問した。情報の小さな変更が、集団に入ることを楽にし得るとリサは気づいた。

paragraphs.english: During a class discussion about school uniforms, Mr. Lee noticed that the same four students answered most questions. Other students listened, but he could not tell whether they agreed or had different ideas. He first tried asking everyone to speak in turn. Several students simply repeated the previous answer because they had not prepared their own words. Mr. Lee changed the next discussion. Before anyone spoke, he gave the class one quiet minute to write down an opinion and a reason. [1] Then students compared notes with a partner before talking to the whole class. More hands went up than before. One quiet student pointed out that buying sports clothes and regular uniforms could cost families a lot. Her idea led to a useful discussion of prices. Mr. Lee kept the writing time in later lessons. He did not expect every student to become a confident speaker immediately, but he wanted everyone to have a fair chance to think.
paragraphs.translation: 制服についての話し合い中、リー先生は大半の質問に同じ四人が答えていると気づいた。他の生徒は聞いていたが、先生は賛成なのか、別の考えがあるのか分からなかった。まず全員に順番に発言してもらおうとした。自分の言葉を用意していなかったため、何人かは前の答えをそのまま繰り返した。リー先生は次の話し合いを変えた。誰かが話す前に、意見と理由を書く静かな一分間をクラスに与えた。これで、生徒は自分の答えを考える時間を持てた。それからクラス全体に話す前に、隣の相手とメモを比べた。以前より多くの手が挙がった。普段静かな生徒が、体操服と通常の制服の購入は家庭に大きな費用がかかり得ると指摘した。その意見は、価格についての有意義な話し合いにつながった。リー先生は以後の授業でも書く時間を残した。全員がすぐ自信ある話し手になるとは期待しなかったが、皆が公平に考える機会を得ることを望んだ。
